text:
Jules (Product): Quick sync: several pilot customers asked for actionable Optimize guidance — they want per-request cost estimates, automated eval alerts when a prompt set drifts, and clear rollout rules for quantization. Need to nail pilot scope this week.
Arun (Eng): Do we try to over-index on cost savings or focus on quality-safe ops first? Both will sell, but different engineering work.
Talia (Data): Data snapshot: pilot tenants A/B/C show two clusters: repetitive short prompts (cacheable) and batchable long jobs. Cache will hit often for A/B, batching helps C. Link to dashboard: https://redwood.internal/pilot/cost-heatmap
Nate (ML): Quantization ask keeps coming up. My take: include a non-default 8-bit path behind an experimental flag + strict automated eval gating. We can auto-fallback if similarity drops.
Priya (Sales): Customers will sign for batching + cache quickly. Quantization only if we promise measurable quality SLAs. I have 2 customers willing to be pilot testers if we provide a simple report showing cost delta and quality checks per run.
Jules (Product): Proposed Q3 pilot slice (minimal): 1) per-request cost estimator (server-side, conservative) 2) adaptive batching with policy knobs 3) prefix KV cache with TTL and opt-out 4) eval-triggered alerts (customer prompt-sets + detectors). Quantization: opt-in beta.
Arun (Eng): Ballpark dev: cost estimator + UI bits = 2 wks; batching + cache infra = 6 wks; eval-alert pipeline = 3 wks (data infra + rules). Quant gating + safe rollout = additional 4 wks.
Talia (Data): For alerts taxonomy I suggest: - prompt-concordance (embedding sim to golden answers) - style/regression (BLEU-ish metrics where applicable) - token-shift (mean token length change) - latency-surprises (p95 jump). We'll need baseline windows and alert thresholds per customer.
pilot-bot: deploy: optimize-pilot/prod - canary started for tenant-A at 5% traffic :rocket:
Nate (ML): Alert actionability: alerts should tie to suggested mitigations: e.g., re-route to higher-precision model, increase temp, or mark prompt-set as invalid. Avoid noise.
Izzy (SRE): Ops requirements: RBAC for uploaded prompt-sets, retention policy for saved embeddings, cache eviction metrics, and a plan for per-tenant cache warmup during rollout. Also need playbook for immediate rollback of cache layer.
Jules (Product): Draft launch criteria for pilot success: - measurable cost savings: >=12% median token-cost reduction for at least 3 tenants across 30d - false-positive alert rate < 5% on sampled review - no >1.5% degradation on customer key prompt-set (human-audited sample). If quant beta used, we add: maintain <=1% quality delta on gate prompts.
Priya (Sales): I'll confirm which customers will accept the 30d measurement window and get agreements for sampled human review.
Arun (Eng): Example adaptive policy snippet (prototype):
```
policy: "adaptive"
max_batch_ms: 15
min_batch_size: 2
priority_modes: ["latency", "cost"]
cache.prefix_ttl_s: 3600
```
Talia (Data): I'll prepare detector playbook and a small notebook to simulate drift thresholds on historical request traces.
Nate (ML): Canary plan for quant: unit test -> offline eval on customer prompt-set -> limited canary (1-5% traffic) -> monitored window (48h) -> expand if metrics stable. Auto-fallback selector must be in place.
Jules (Product): Decisions: Ship pilot with per-request estimator + adaptive batching + KV prefix cache + eval-triggered alerts. Quantization goes into opt-in beta tied to canary gating. Action owners: @Arun proto + perf sims; @Talia detectors + thresholds; @Nate quant gating doc; @Priya customer signups; @Izzy rollout/rollback runbook. I'll cut a roadmap slice and circulate to leadership.
Priya (Sales): I'll push for pilot funding from two customers; if they fund quant work, we can move it earlier.
Izzy (SRE): Noted. I'll draft an incident playbook focused on alert noise and cache corruption scenarios.
Arun (Eng): Will drop perf sim results and a lightweight config UI mock by Tue EOD.
Jules (Product): Thanks team. Short follow-up: keep the estimator conservative early (overpredict cost rather than underpredict). We'll iterate the estimator after real pilot telemetry.
